messages:
Ivy: starting deploy v2.4.2 into change-window (ap-southeast) 1: initial 8% traffic on embeds and rerank routes. deploy-bot: rollout started id=5980 at 1795012345, routes=[embeds, rerank], traffic=8%

Rex: watching SLOs and tokens per second. @eng-runtime pls watch embed-route p95 and error budget.

SLO-alert-bot: [WARN] embeds-route error-budget burn high: 12% in 5m (threshold 10%) 

eng-runtime: seeing a small cluster of 503s from worker pool gpu-pool-c2 around 13:12 UTC. logs: `2026-03-22T13:12:03Z error: rpc failed: upstream 503 backpressure`

Ivy: is this persistent or a spike? Any latency signal?

Rex: p95 for embeds up from 140ms -> 410ms for that window. token throughput down ~15%.

eng-runtime: looks correlated to a recent kernel eviction policy change in v2.4.2 on that pool. Suggest we offload embeds to fallback pool (gpu-pool-b) and reduce traffic to problematic pool. We can do targeted traffic-split instead of pinning.

Ivy: agree to targeted split. deploy-bot run a traffic-shift: move embeds 90% -> gpu-pool-b, keep 10% on original for metrics. execute `deployctl split --route=embeds --from=gpu-pool-c2 --to=gpu-pool-b --percent=90`

deploy-bot: executing split... success at 1795012400. embeds now 90% on gpu-pool-b, 10% on gpu-pool-c2. Monitoring.

SLO-alert-bot: [INFO] embeds p95 dropped to 160ms after split, error-budget burn down to 6%

Rex: good immediate effect. eng-runtime, can you roll a quick kernel flag revert on pool-c2 while we keep split? We want to validate without user-facing impact.

eng-runtime: preparing revert CL and smoke test. ETA ~12m. Uploading traces for the spike: https://s3.redwood/5980/trace-embed-13-12.json

Ivy: release-notes-bot add note: "During change window v2.4.2 canary, observed gpu-pool-c2 503/backpressure affecting embeds; traffic split to fallback pool; no customer-facing errors observed; follow-up RCA planned."

release-notes-bot: PR updated https://git.redwood/release-notes/pulls/349 at 1795012465

Rex: decision: keep split for 20m, validate reverted kernel on c2, then either re-merge traffic or pin embeds to stable if instability persists. Any objections?

Ivy: none. Also create an incident ticket and add eng-sre for deeper correlation to autoscaler and network queue metrics.

eng-runtime: revert patch rolled to c2 at 1795012498, running smoke checks. so far no errors in smoke.

SLO-alert-bot: [OK] embeds error-budget burn returning to baseline (4%). p95 stable ~150ms.

Ivy: great, schedule traffic-merge back in 10m if metrics hold. Leaving thread open for final merge. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
